title: Temporary capacity extension: notification, grace-periods, and finalization workflow
creator: Maya Chen
description: Introduce a controlled temporary capacity extension mechanism that enables Dedicated customers to receive short-lived surge headroom (extension) with clear UI visibility, audit logs, and deterministic billing finalization. This ticket focuses on the user-visible notification/grace period workflow, final settlement behavior for overage invoices, and the server-side finalization hooks used by the autoscaler and billing reconciler.
background: Customers have asked for predictable short bursts beyond reserved capacity (surge headroom) while avoiding surprise invoices or ambiguous chargeback. Current surge pools provide ephemeral capacity but lack a uniform notification and finalization lifecycle: users see no clear countdown, invoices can show provisional charges, and support tickets increase when customers dispute overages. We need a clear extension lifecycle: grant -> notify -> grace -> finalize (or roll back) with deterministic billing adjustments and auditability.
acceptance_criteria: API/Console shows active temporary extensions with start, TTL, and remaining headroom
Customers can opt-in/off auto-finalize; default behavior finalizes to the nearest billable unit with transparent invoice line-items
Billing reconciler produces a human-readable adjustment when provisional charges change after finalization
Audit log entry for each extension lifecycle event (granted, notified, grace-entered, finalized, rolled-back)
End-to-end tests verifying that capacity is reclaimed after TTL expiry and that autoscaler respects temporary headroom during scaling decisions
design_notes: Extension token model: server issues a single-time-use extension token with TTL and capacity_quota. Token is referenced in autoscaler decision path to temporarily increase target headroom.
Notification model: Console push + email for accounts with billing contact; webhook event (extension.updated) for programmatic consumers

Grace period semantics: when TTL expires, enter a 10-minute grace window where requests are allowed but flagged as 'post-extension' for reconciliation. During this window, customers can request an appeal or purchase extension; otherwise finalization runs.

Finalization behavior: compute actual extra tokens used during the extension window, apply pricing rules (metered at surge rate), generate a provisional invoice line, and mark as pending until reconciliation job completes
Fail-safes: if billing reconciler fails, extension remains in 'finalizing' state and automated fallback reduces headroom progressively to avoid indefinite extra cost
implementation_plan: [API] Add POST /dedicated/extensions to issue extension tokens (backend: extensions-service) -- 2pts
[Autoscaler] Accept extension token in scale decision flow and treat capacity_quota as transient headroom -- 2pts
[Billing] Add provisional_line_item and finalization state to billing pipeline, integrate with reconciler -- 3pts
[Console] Display active extensions, TTL, remaining headroom, and finalization status; add 'request extension' flow in Capacity page -- 3pts
[Telemetry] Emit extension lifecycle events to metrics pipeline; dashboard for active extensions and reconciliation latency -- 1pt
[Docs] PRD + customer-facing docs describing behavior and pricing -- 1pt
rollout_plan: Feature-flag all new endpoints and console UI behind ff:dedicated-temporary-extensions
Canary: enable for internal + 3 pilot customers in us-west for 1 week; collect reconciliation latency and dispute rate
Regional ramp: enable in EU region next week if metrics stable
GA: open to all dedicated customers and surface opt-in in console
Post-GA: 30-day review to consider defaults (e.g., grace window length, surge rate) based on dispute frequency
testing_notes: Unit tests for token lifecycle, integration tests between autoscaler and extensions-service, end-to-end billing reconciliation tests using synthetic traffic traces to validate invoice adjustments. Load tests for surge scenarios to ensure temporary headroom doesn't violate SLOs. Add regression tests to prevent permanent headroom leaks after finalization.
